original_question: Is the fundamental group of a closed manifold without conjugate points semihyperbolic?
target_in_paper: Question 4.1.3 in Section 4.1 ("Relations between these concepts"): "Is the fundamental group of a closed manifold without conjugate points semihyperbolic?" on page 9. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim: it has the same hypothesis (a closed manifold without conjugate points), the same object of interest (the fundamental group), and the same target property (semihyperbolicity). ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the metric should be named explicitly: in Section 4 the setting is Riemannian, so "without conjugate points" refers to a Riemannian metric g on M with no conjugate points. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
The paper's standing notation assumes that M is a connected C-infinity manifold. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
A self-contained rewrite should denote the group explicitly by pi_1(M), rather than only saying "the fundamental group."

Because the survey does not define semihyperbolicity at this point, the stand-alone version should specify "semihyperbolic in the sense of Alonso-Bridson." ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a closed connected C-infinity Riemannian manifold without conjugate points. Must its fundamental group pi_1(M) be semihyperbolic in the sense of Alonso-Bridson?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Question 4.1.3, not the broader neighboring Question 4.1.2 about whether M carries a metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. The surrounding discussion in Section 4.1 explains that the authors are comparing manifolds with no conjugate points to manifolds of nonpositive curvature, and then they single out semihyperbolicity as one of the specific open problems they mention from Section 8 of [Iva-Kap2014]. The sentence immediately after Question 4.1.3 provides the only extra local clarification in the survey: semihyperbolicity is the Alonso-Bridson notion intended to capture large-scale nonpositive curvature. No equivalent reformulation is proved in the paper, so the faithful refinement is simply to make the metric, notation, and reference sense of semihyperbolic explicit without broadening the problem. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
